items.title: The Death Of The Button: Why The Best Interface Is No Interface
items.summary_original: Ever since the commercialisation of the Graphical User Interface pioneered by systems like the Xerox Star and popularised by the original Apple Macintosh , software has relied heavily on point-and-click interactions. If you wanted to book a trip, buy a pair of shoes, or research a health symptom, you were expected to navigate a labyrinth of user interfaces. You click menus, adjust range sliders, fill out multi-step forms, deal with cookie pop-ups, and open dozens of browser tabs just to cross-reference basic information. We have become accustomed to spending more time managing the software rather than actually achieving our goals. That contract is officially changing. items.title_de: Der Tod des Knopfes: Warum die beste Schnittstelle keine Schnittstelle ist
items.summary_de: Seit der Kommerzialisierung der grafischen Benutzeroberfläche, die durch Systeme wie den Xerox Star vorangetrieben und durch den ursprünglichen Apple Macintosh populär gemacht wurde, ist Software stark auf Point-and-Click-Interaktionen angewiesen. Wenn Sie eine Reise buchen, ein Paar Schuhe kaufen oder ein Gesundheitssymptom recherchieren wollten, wurde von Ihnen erwartet, dass Sie sich durch ein Labyrinth von Benutzeroberflächen navigieren. Sie klicken auf Menüs, passen Bereichsregler an, füllen mehrstufige Formulare aus, kümmern sich um Cookie-Popups und öffnen Dutzende Browser-Registerkarten, nur um grundlegende Informationen zu vergleichen. Wir haben uns daran gewöhnt, mehr Zeit mit der Verwaltung der Software zu verbringen, als dass wir unsere Ziele tatsächlich erreichen. Dieser Vertrag ändert sich offiziell. Angetrieben durch Fortschritte in der künstlichen Intelligenz und großen Sprachmodellen ist eine neue Generation von Web-Tools auf dem Vormarsch

items.summary_original: When the Dance Floor Became the Stage Looking back at Vitra Design Museum’s 2018 exhibition Night Fever, the history of club culture reveals a recurring architectural experiment: what happens when the audience is no longer separate from the spectacle? A nightclub does not have a conventional audience. There is no fixed row of seats, no clear division between stage and auditorium, and no guarantee that the person who enters will remain a spectator. Once inside, bodies, sound, light, fashion and architecture begin to become one. The room changes as people move, and the people inside are part of what everyone else is experiencing. items.summary_original: Paul Chan turns cultural memory into a retail interior Studio Paul Chan completes LANG’s 110-square-meter flagship at ROW DTLA in Los Angeles , transforming a former industrial warehouse into a fashion store and cultural venue shaped by the experience of living between cultures. Karolina Zolubak zeigt in zwei Stunden, wie Profil, Netzwerk und Content zusammenspielen – und wie daraus eine LinkedIn-Strategie für den eigenen Arbeitsalltag entsteht. Viele Kreative sind auf LinkedIn zwar angemeldet, nutzen die Plattform aber nicht strategisch. Das Profil gleicht einem digitalen Lebenslauf, das Netzwerk ist eher zufällig gewachsen und beim Thema Content fehlt oft ein Plan. Centered on the theme ‘Design for Humanity at Play,’ the award invites designers, brands, and institutions participating in Expo 2027 Belgrade to submit projects developed between January 01, 2023 and December 31, 2026. Framing play as a vital mechanism for connection and speculative thinking, the competition challenges the creative community to explore how design can foster connection, participation, and resilience across nine distinct project categories. items.summary_original: The reaction to McLaren's new identity has been loud and largely negative. Having spent two years as its head of brand, I don't think the objections are really about a logo. In 1970 the Rolling Stones were apparently booed off stage. The crime? They played Brown Sugar. The crowd had never heard the song (it wouldn't be released until the following year) and they were there for the established hits. Whether the story is apocryphal or not, I was reminded of it last week by the reaction to McLaren's rebrand . The reaction has been considerable, subjective and largely negative. items.title_de: Ich habe die Marke McLaren mitgeprägt. Das ist es, was mich an der Aktualisierung beunruhigt
items.summary_de: Die Reaktion auf McLarens neue Identität war laut und größtenteils negativ. Nachdem ich zwei Jahre als Markenchef gearbeitet habe, glaube ich nicht, dass es bei den Einwänden wirklich um ein Logo geht. 1970 wurden die Rolling Stones offenbar außerhalb der Bühne ausgebuht. Das Verbrechen? Sie spielten Brown Sugar. Das Publikum hatte das Lied noch nie gehört (es sollte erst im folgenden Jahr veröffentlicht werden) und war wegen der etablierten Hits da. Ob die Geschichte apokryph ist oder nicht, ich wurde letzte Woche durch die Reaktion auf McLarens Rebranding daran erinnert. Die Reaktion war beträchtlich, subjektiv und größtenteils negativ. Ironischerweise zeichnet sich McLaren dadurch aus, dass er sich weigert, stehen zu bleiben. Ein Unternehmen, das mehr als sechzig Jahre damit verbracht hat, Dinge besser, schneller, leichter und effizienter zu machen, oft durch die Weiterentwicklung bereits Außergewöhnlicher

items.title: The DFB-Pokal Reimagined
items.summary_original: The DFB-Pokal thrives on contrast: professional clubs facing semi-professional sides, favourites meeting underdogs, and decades of tradition colliding with stories that can unfold in a single night. Its new visual identity seeks to make that tension visible. Introduced for the 2026/27 season, the rebrand brings the men’s, women’s and junior competitions into a shared design system while giving each its own character and expression. At the heart of the new approach is a fundamental question: how can a brand built on consistency capture a competition defined by unpredictability? In this interview, Holger Merk, Head of Brand Department, discusses the thinking behind the new identity, the role of contrast, the balance between tradition and digital culture, and how design can create a framework

items.title: Lingo
items.summary_original: Imagine a library. Sealed-in quiet, walls thick as dictionaries. But that's not why you're here — you're at the computer, navigating to your personal linguistic authority: Urban Dictionary. Feverishly typing in the word on your mind since it left your crush's lips in math class: turnt. A thrill washes over you. Not just the definition, but the sight of it: turnt, turned from spoken to serif. Dignified. Elevated. To see slang suited up feels almost subversive. And just right. That's where Softdrive's new typeface, Lingo, comes from. Timeless elegance meets current trend, intellectual authority meets the people's slang. Lingo is both a workhorse, trotting along in body copy, and a show pony, shining in display. This serif respects classical typographic tradition... until it doesn't. Lingo ha

items.summary_original: the path of the runway rewritten Fashion shows typically begin with a straightforward diagram. Models move along a prescribed path, its edges lined with spectators, and everyone knows where to look. In general this basic layout has remained consistent across time. Yet some of the strongest runway sets begin by disturbing that diagram. Across four decades, designers and scenographers have buried the catwalk beneath the floor, broken it into a grid, or removed the act of walking all together. In these shows, set design shapes much more than just a decorative backdrop. It determines when a model appears and how long they stay visible. items.summary_original: ETH ZURICH TRAINS ROBOTIC HAND TO WALK ON ITS FINGERS A robotic hand has apparently decided it no longer needs the rest of the robot . Researchers at ETH Zurich’s Soft Robotics Lab have developed an autonomous five-fingered hand that can walk across different surfaces, steer itself, recover after falling over and interact with objects — all using the same fingers normally reserved for grasping. Rather than adding wheels or legs to the system, the team turns the hand itself into a mobile robot, allowing its fingers to alternate between supporting, moving and manipulating its body. The prototype is based on a commercially available anthropomorphic hand equipped with five fingers and 20 actuated joints, four for each finger. items.summary_original: Nils Leonard explains how painstaking craft turned a collection of annoying buzzwords into a parody of the periodic table, a campaign that's now won design and advertising's biggest award. items.summary_original: To be completely honest with you, I missed the news when CSS Container Queries first shipped. And when I finally heard about it, my very first thought was, “Why exactly do I need this when media queries already exist?” I’m not proud of that reaction, knowing what I know now, but it was comforting to know that I wasn’t alone. In fact, there are legions of us out there. What baffles me is that container queries aren’t a new feature, as it currently sits at around 94% browser support . And yet, very few people are actually using it. According to the State of CSS survey, 86% of developers are aware of container queries, but only 41.4% actually use them. items.summary_original: turning Silence, Emptiness and Absence Into Art We may be used to thinking of art as something that asks us to look. Still, some of the most influential experiments in postwar art began by questioning this basic expectation, asking what could happen if an artist withheld the very elements that make an artwork visible or audible. These works leave space for something less obvious to come through, whether that is the changing light of a room , the sounds of an audience, the physical character of architecture or just the awareness of one’s own body occupying a particular place at a particular time.
